newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eight Algerians burnt alive in rebel raid - paper.
newsitem.headline: Eight Algerians burnt alive in rebel raid - paper.

text.p: Eight villagers were burnt alive and five more had their throats cut by suspected Moslem rebels who attacked a remote hamlet in northern Algeria at the weekend, an Algerian newspaper said on Sunday.

Al Alam Assiassi Arab language newspaper said the rebels also kidnapped a young man after the Saturday massacre, which the newspaper said could have been worse if most of the hamlet inhabitants had not fled at the advance of the guerrillas.

A first group attacked a house near the local police station to divert security forces' attention, the paper said. A second group stormed houses at the other end of the village, setting ablaze homes in which eight people were burnt alive.
The attackers cut the throats of five more villagers before leaving, the newspaper said. The victims included babies and elderly people, it added.
The killings took place in a hamlet between Douaouda and Kolea towns in Tipaza costal province, 60 km (40 miles) west of Algiers, said Al Alam Assiassi.
The reported attack was the latest in a series of massacres the authorities blame on Moslem guerrillas trying to topple Algeria's moderate secular government.
Algeria's first plural National Assembly was due to open later on Sunday with Moslem fundamentalists and well as secualrists represented following the June 5 general election.

More than 90 villagers were slaughtered by Moslem guerrillas last month in the worst massacre in five-and-a-half years of violence following the cancellation of the last general election in which Moslem fundamentalists had taken a commanding lead..
